home.nothingNeedsYou: Nothing needs you. Tasks that need a reply, logins to reconnect and change requests to review appear here.
home.nothingRunning: No task is running. Label an issue or ask in Chat.
setup.intro: Set up {tenant}: do these in order. When the last step is done, the first task appears and this page becomes your dashboard. Nothing is installed in your repositories.
setup.step1: 1 · Link GitHub and install the App
setup.step1Done: Linked as {login}. Installed on {account} · {n} repositories selected
setup.step1Todo: Link your GitHub account, then install the GitHub App on the account that owns your repositories.
setup.step2Detail: An empty repository you own, {repo}. Triggers, skills and projects live here.
setup.step3Detail: Use your subscription or an API key.
setup.step4Detail: Pick the template “labeled issue → agent → pull requests with green checks” and the repository. sanchoris opens a pull request with it on your config repository. Merge it on GitHub.
setup.step5Detail: Add the label to an issue. The first task starts.
setup.projectDetail: Group repositories that one agent works on together, such as a frontend and a backend.
setup.slackDetail: Ask for work from a channel or DM.
setup.connectSubscriptionDetail: Run this on your machine and sign in. The login is registered with your account.
setup.name: Name
setup.usedBySessionDetail: A session names the credential it uses. Name it here when you save it.
triggers.intro: A trigger starts a task: an agent session that must run its required skills to the end. {n} triggers, {changes} change request open. A chat trigger names the scope of the chat: all projects, or one project.
triggers.issueLabeled: A GitHub issue gets the label {labels} from {senders}.
triggers.issueComment: A comment is added to a GitHub issue by {senders}.
triggers.children: Children: depth {depth}, up to {count} per task.
triggers.checkRun: A GitHub check run fails on a pull request in {repos}
triggers.labelNotAllowed: label added by {login}, who is not in the pattern
triggers.senderNotAllowed: sent by {login}, who is not in the pattern
triggers.duplicate: a task with the same name exists
triggers.noEvents: No events yet. Events appear when a trigger receives an issue, a message or a schedule.
triggers.empty: No triggers yet. Use New from template to open a pull request on your config repository.
triggers.footer: Triggers are YAML in your config repositories. Edit them on GitHub. The On switch is the state of the trigger (ENABLED, DISABLED).
triggers.proposed: Opened change request {link}. Merge it on GitHub.
skills.intro: A skill is a procedure the agent can call. A reliable skill runs its fixed steps outside the session, so it finishes the same way every time.
skills.empty: No skills yet. Add a folder under skills/ in your config repository.
skills.footer: Skills are folders in your config repository: {skillMd} for the agent, and {skillYaml} for the steps sanchoris runs. A skill without {skillYaml} is plain: the agent reads it, and a trigger cannot require it.
skill.plainNote: This skill is plain: it has SKILL.md only, so the agent reads it and no steps run.
chat.pickSession: Pick the session to chat in. Its agent works in the session's repositories and can run its skills.
chat.noConfig: A chat runs in a session of your config. Install the GitHub App and add a config repository in
chat.noSessions: The config has no session. Add one to sanchoris.yaml; see
chat.continueHint: The last task has finished. Your next message starts task {n} in the same conversation.
notify.approval: The agent is waiting for your approval.
notify.question: The agent asked you a question.
rewind.title: Edit from here?
rewind.body: Rewind chat to before this message. Your prompt and attachments return to the composer. "Revert files too" also undoes the agent's edits since then.
chat.tooManyAttachments: You can attach up to {n} images per message.
queue.title: Queued
queue.sendNowHint: Start a turn with this message
chat.issuesFiledDetail: Each issue started its own task, asynchronously.
chat.filedHint: Issues the agent files from a chat appear here. Each one starts its own task.
diff.truncated: The diff is cut here because it is long.
work.startingSession: Waiting for a session to start
mode.buildHint: Default mode — click to enter plan mode
mode.planHint: Plan mode — click to return to normal build mode
mode.supervisedDetail: Ask before commands and file changes.
mode.acceptEditsDetail: Auto-approve edits, ask before other actions.
mode.fullAccessDetail: Allow commands and edits without prompts.
context.label: Context {percent} full
context.hint: {used} of {max} tokens of context in use. Send /compact, optionally followed by what the summary should keep, to have the agent summarize the conversation and continue from the summary.
context.autoCompact: Compacts on its own when the chat stays idle for {minutes} min after a reply that leaves the context {percent}% full or more.
context.autoCompactOff: Automatic compaction is off for this session. Set AutoCompact (IdleMinutes, ContextPercent) on the session in the config to turn it on.
chat.autoCompactedHint: The chat stayed idle with its context filling up, so sanchoris sent /compact.
tasks.intro: {n} tasks. Needs-you items come first. Each task shows where its required skill stands.
tasks.empty: Tasks are empty. Label an issue, or ask in Chat.
task.nudgesExhausted: {skill} did not succeed after the reminders
task.approvalRequested: The skill asks for your approval
task.usageLimitManual: Usage limit reached; resume by hand
task.workspaceStopped: The workspace stopped before the task finished
task.fromChat: from a chat in the session {session}
task.messageGoes: Your message goes to the agent session, and the skill runs again.
task.messageGoesAgent: Your message goes to the agent session.
task.messagePlaceholder: Skip the flaky test and fix the cause in the cart fixture.
task.stopBody: The agent session and its workspace stop, and the task ends as Stopped. A stopped task cannot be resumed.
task.approvalNote: Approve to let the skill go on, or reject to fail this step of the skill.
task.noSkillRuns: The agent has not called a skill yet.
run.title: Run {n}
run.rateLimitAllowed: the worker's usage is within its limit
run.rateLimitWarning: the worker's usage is close to its limit
run.rateLimitRejected: the worker reached its usage limit
run.rateLimitOther: the worker reported usage limit status {status}
run.stopBody: The agent session of this run and its workspace stop.
integrations.intro: Your GitHub account, the GitHub App and Slack: the places work comes from and reports to.
integrations.linkedAs: Linked as {login}. sanchoris matches a GitHub user to a member by this login, so a session can use the credential of the member who asked.
integrations.notLinked: Link your GitHub account so sanchoris can match your GitHub activity to you.
integrations.notInstalled: Install the GitHub App on the account that owns your repositories.
integrations.slackDetail: Ask for work from a channel or DM. Optional.
integrations.slackLater: Slack comes later; it is not available yet.
integrations.outcome.inUse: This GitHub account is linked to another user.
integrations.outcome.requested: GitHub sent the installation request to an owner of the account. The installation shows here after they approve it.
integrations.outcome.notMember: You are not a member of this tenant.
integrations.outcome.notAdmin: Only an owner or an admin can install the GitHub App.
integrations.outcome.notLinked: Link your GitHub account before you install the App.
integrations.outcome.notLinkedAccount: You installed the App as a GitHub user other than your linked account. Sign in to GitHub as the linked account and install again.
integrations.outcome.notAccessible: Your GitHub account cannot see this installation.
integrations.outcome.notAdminOfAccount: Only an admin of the GitHub account that owns the installation can connect it.
integrations.outcome.installationInUse: This installation is connected to another tenant.
integrations.outcome.denied: GitHub did not grant access, so nothing changed.
config.intro: Git repositories that hold your triggers, skills and projects. Edit and review changes on GitHub.
config.removeHint: To remove a config, remove its repository from the GitHub App installation on GitHub. The config is then disabled: its triggers stop, its sessions and projects leave these screens, and its unfinished tasks are stopped.
config.disabledHint: The config no longer syncs or starts tasks. Add the repository to the GitHub App installation again and add it as a new config to use it.
config.projectsDetail: A project groups repositories that one agent works on together. A session on a single repository names the repository and needs no project.
credentials.intro: Claude and Codex logins and keys. Each has a name that sessions refer to.
credentials.empty: No credentials yet. Connect a subscription or save an API key.
credentials.howPicked: How a session picks a credential
credentials.howPickedDetail: A session names the credential it uses, for example {example}. Writing {requester} uses the personal credential of the member who asked, or for a GitHub event the member who linked the GitHub account of its sender, and fails if there is no such member or that member has none.
members.intro: {n} of {total} members in {tenant}. Invitations count while they are pending.
members.introNoLimit: {n} members in {tenant}, with no limit. Invitations count while they are pending.
members.footer: Owners and admins invite, change roles and remove members. A session names the credential it uses, so members do not need their own.
audit.intro: Who did what in {tenant}. Entries are append-only. Owners and admins can read and export them.
billing.intro: Plan and usage for {tenant}. Paid plans are billed monthly in USD through Stripe.
billing.adminIntro: {tenant} is on the Admin plan, which a tenant gets when a verified @sancode.dev email creates it. Tasks, workspace hours and members have no limit, nothing is billed, and the plan does not change.
checkout.tenantPaid: Stripe took the payment. The tenant becomes active when Stripe confirms it.
checkout.tenantCanceled: You canceled the checkout, so the tenant was not created.
checkout.planPaid: Stripe took the payment. The new plan applies when Stripe confirms it.
checkout.planCanceled: You canceled the checkout, so the plan did not change.
tenantState.paymentPending: This tenant waits for its payment. Tasks start after Stripe confirms the checkout.
tenantState.paymentFailed: This tenant is suspended because the last payment failed. Update the payment method in Stripe.
billing.thresholds: you are told at 80% · new tasks wait at 100%
billing.footer: The price covers the whole tenant, whatever the number of members. One task is one issue, one chat thread, or one scheduled run. Workspace hours count the time a workspace is running, not the time a task waits. Change or cancel the plan at any time. Agents run on your own Claude and Codex subscriptions or API keys, so model usage is not billed here. Invoices and the payment method are in Stripe.
billing.deleteTenantNote: Stops the tenant's tasks, cancels its subscription, and removes its configs, credentials, tasks, runs and session records. Audit events stay until their retention ends.
billing.deleteTenantBody: Its unfinished tasks stop now and its subscription is cancelled. Its data and session records are then deleted. This cannot be undone.
billing.deleteTenantFree: Your account keeps using its one Free tenant: deleting this tenant does not let you create another Free tenant.
operator.intro: {n} tenants · {workspaces} live workspaces · {hours} run hours and {revenue} revenue this month. Create, suspend and bill customers. Visible to the operator only.
operator.notOperator: This page is for sanchoris operators.
cli.title: Approve sancli
cli.intro: A sancli command on your machine waits for this approval. Check that the code matches the one in your terminal.
cli.unknown: No sancli request has the code {code}. Check the code, or run the command again.
cli.claude: {client} asks to add your Claude subscription (the token from claude setup-token) as a credential.
cli.codex: {client} asks to add your Codex login (~/.codex/auth.json) as a credential.
cli.warning: Approve only a command that you ran yourself: the approved command adds a credential to this tenant.
cli.approved: Approved. Return to the terminal: sancli finishes the registration.
cli.denied: Denied. sancli stops without adding anything.
cli.expired: The code expired. Run the command again.
cli.noTenant: You are not a member of a tenant yet.
tenantNew.title: Create tenant
tenantNew.intro: A tenant is the place where your team’s tasks, triggers and billing live. You can invite people after it exists.
tenantNew.limitsTotal: {tasks} tasks and {hours} workspace hours in total
tenantNew.noLimits: no limit on tasks, workspace hours or members
tenantNew.createAndPay: Create tenant and pay in Stripe
tenantNew.afterPayment: After payment you install the GitHub App and connect Claude or Codex.
tenantNew.afterCreate: The tenant is created at once. Next you install the GitHub App and connect Claude or Codex.
login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in with your Google account. You link GitHub later, in Settings.
login.after: New here? Signing in creates your account, and then you create a tenant or join one.
login.failed: Sign-in failed: {error}. Going back to sign in…
reason.ownerPlan: Only owners can change the plan.
reason.ownerPortal: Only owners can open billing in Stripe.
reason.ownerDelete: Only owners can delete the tenant.
reason.adminTriggers: Only owners and admins can turn triggers on or off.
reason.adminConfigs: Only owners and admins can add and sync configs.
reason.adminOrgKey: Only owners and admins can add keys for the organization.
reason.adminCredential: Only owners and admins can change the credentials of other members and of the organization.
reason.adminMembers: Only owners and admins can invite members and revoke invitations.
reason.adminAudit: Only owners and admins can read the audit log.
reason.adminInstall: Only owners and admins can install the GitHub App.
reason.adminSlack: Only owners and admins can add Slack.
reason.approval: Only owners, admins and the member who asked for the task can answer this approval.
reason.runNotChat: Only runs of a chat take messages.
reason.slackThread: Reply to this thread in Slack.
reason.agentWorking: Wait until the agent finishes its turn.
reason.rewindWhileWorking: Interrupt the current turn before reverting checkpoints.
reason.rewindJoinedTurn: This message went into a turn an earlier message started. Edit from that message instead.
reason.questionUnanswered: Pick an option or type an answer first.
reason.noSession: Add a config with a session first.
reason.noTriggers: There are no triggers to filter by.
reason.noSkills: There are no skills with a skill.yaml to filter by.
reason.noActions: There are no actions in this period.
reason.proposeNeeds: Add a config and a repository of the GitHub App first.
reason.noRepository: Add a repository to the GitHub App installation first.
reason.connectOpen: The connection steps are open above.
reason.suspendOpen: The suspend form is open below.
